failure: Found in testing: a caller who goes silent is never closed. One reprompt, then the call stays open indefinitely (cost and a blocked line).
design: reprompt at 8s and 16s of silence, close at 44s (a callback task is recorded first if work is pending)
cause: the handler acted once, on the user 'away' event only, so the second reprompt and the close never fired
fix: a one-second timer runs while the caller is silent (ava/guards.py silence_step, ava/voice/agent.py), plus an offline eval of the schedule

before.label: 1 real phone test call, synthetic, 2026-11-11, old handler
before.result: one reprompt about 8s after the greeting reply, then 45s more of silence with no close; the caller hung up at 68s

after.label: 1 simulated-caller test call (WebRTC, synthetic voice), fixed handler, not a phone call
after.result: replied to hello, reprompted at 8s and again 8s later, said goodbye and ended the call itself at 44s of silence
after.server_log: silence_reprompt n=1, silence_reprompt n=2, silence_close action=end, call_end reason=silence_end, 0 appointments
after.not_measured: the fixed handler on a real phone call

discarded: one earlier simulated run overlapped a deployment, so the old container was replaced mid-call; it is not counted as evidence in either direction
